stem.text: Let \( f(x) = \frac{24}{5 - x} \). The Taylor series for f about \( x = 1 \) is \( \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} 6 \left(\frac{x - 1}{4}\right)^{n} \). Its radius of convergence is \( 4 \). Does the series converge to f at \( x = -3 \)? Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: No, because \( x = -3 \) is an endpoint that the interval of convergence \( -3 < x < 5 \) excludes.

worked_solution.text: The ratio test gives convergence for \( \left|x - 1\right| < 4 \), the interior \( -3 < x < 5 \), and \( x = -3 \) is an endpoint.
At \( x = -3 \) the series is \( \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} 6 (-1)^{n} \), whose terms do not approach 0, so it diverges there. The interval of convergence is \( -3 < x < 5 \).

options.label: Yes, because the series converges to f at every point where f is defined.
